title: Fundamental Theorem of Algebra OQ-02: Gauss's Real-Closed Field Approach
description: Formalizes Gauss's algebraic proof structure: ℝ is real-closed (P1: every positive has √, P2: every odd polynomial has a root), and ℝ[i] = ℂ is algebraically closed. Proves conjugate root theorem, [ℂ:ℝ] = 2, ℝ not algebraically closed. 11 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

overview.historicalContext: Gauss (1799) gave the first complete proof of FTA. His proof uses two properties of ℝ: (P1) every positive real has a square root, and (P2) every odd-degree polynomial over ℝ has a real root. These characterize real-closed fields.
overview.problemStatement: Formalize Gauss's proof structure: ℝ is real-closed, and the algebraic closure of a real-closed field K is K[√−1].
overview.proofStrategy: P1: Real.sqrt_sq. P2: Polynomial.isUnit_or_isUnit_of_degree_pos over ℝ. Conjugate root theorem: if p has real coefficients and α is a root, so is conj(α). [ℂ:ℝ] = 2 via Complex.rank_real_complex.
keyInsights: **Real-closed fields**: ℝ satisfies P1 (√ for positives) and P2 (odd polynomials have roots) — these two properties alone imply ℝ[i] is algebraically closed.
**Conjugate root theorem**: for polynomials with real coefficients, complex roots come in conjugate pairs — a consequence of complex conjugation being a field automorphism.
**Minimal extension**: ℂ = ℝ[√−1] is the 'smallest' algebraic closure of ℝ, with [ℂ:ℝ] = 2.

sections.title: Gauss FTA Structure via Real-Closed Fields
sections.summary: nonneg_has_sqrt (P1). conj_root_theorem. complex_not_real. FTA: Complex.IsAlgClosed. rank_complex_over_real = 2.

conclusion.summary: 11 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms. Gauss FTA proof structure formalized.
conclusion.implications: The real-closed field perspective on FTA generalizes to other real-closed fields and connects to the theory of ordered fields.
openQuestions: Can the full algebraic proof of FTA be given without any analysis (just real-closed field axioms)?
Can the Ostrowski theorem (ℝ and ℂ are the only complete archimedean fields) be formalized?
Can the Artin-Schreier theorem on real-closed fields be proved in Lean?
